newsitem.title: UK: Research finds potential for industry rapemeal use.
newsitem.headline: Research finds potential for industry rapemeal use.

text.p: Industrial markets for rapemeal could be developed in the European Union to bypass an agreement with the United States that restricts feed use, a research funded by the UK's Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said Wednesday.

"...Blair House restrictions...imposed a ceiling on the amount of industrial oilseeds that could be grown in the EU. One solution is to ensure that the meal is used for non-feed purposes," said HGCA in a statement.
The Blair House agreement, signed between EU and U.S., limits the animal feed derived from oilseeds grown on set-aside land to one million tonnes of soya bean meal equivalent.
The HGCA report said non-feed markets for rapeseed meal could amount to "a significant tonnage" with only minimal investment in research.
One area of rapemeal use was speciality fertiliser, it said, while more extensive work was recommended for such uses as cat litter, oil absorbents and composites.
There was also potential industrial uses from the protein contained in rapemeal, for example, in adhesives and paper coatings, the research concluded.
